title: Identity-point composition normalization at all coefficient stages
statement:
Fix a six-functor datum [def-sf-datum], with $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $n\geq1$. Put $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ and choose $\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\}$. Let $X$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme, $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, and $a:X\to s$ its structure morphism. Use the datum's constructible finite-Tor categories and exceptional adjunctions; at the integral stage use the specified completed operations with compatible etale-origin witnesses on finite reductions, at $E$ their raw scalar localization, and at $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ their common finite coefficient stages, on the corresponding domains of [fix-lem-exchanges]. Write $I=R\mathrm{id}_{s!}$ and $J=R\mathrm{id}_s^!$. Let $\alpha_{\mathrm{id}_s,a}:IRa_!\xrightarrow{\sim}Ra_!$ be the specified compact-support composition comparison: at finite coefficients the comparison of [thm-sf-comp-composition], integrally the specified completed comparison of [fix-lem-exchanges](2),(4), and at field coefficients its scalar-localized or common-stage image as in the same node. Let $v:I\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathrm{id}$ be the canonical identity comparison: finite-level identity compactification, integrally the inverse of the actual reduction/total-limit unit $u_C:C\to\mathcal L_s\mathcal R_sC$ of [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus], and at field coefficients its scalar image. Then $\alpha_{\mathrm{id}_s,a}=vRa_!$; equivalently it is the identity under this comparison at every listed coefficient stage.

Let $e:IJ\to\mathrm{id}$ be the counit of $I\dashv J$, put $\omega_s=J\Lambda_s$, and define the identity-normalized counit
$$\nu=e_{\Lambda_s}\circ v_{J\Lambda_s}^{-1}:\omega_s\longrightarrow\Lambda_s.$$
Let $c:Ra^!\omega_s\to Ra^!\Lambda_s$ be the inverse of the right-adjoint mate of $\alpha_{\mathrm{id}_s,a}$; equivalently it is the conjugate of $\alpha_{\mathrm{id}_s,a}^{-1}$ with respect to $Ra_!\dashv Ra^!$ and the composite adjunction $IRa_!\dashv Ra^!J$, with pasted unit and counit. Then $\nu$ and $c$ are isomorphisms, $c=Ra^!(\nu)$, and, for the counit $\varepsilon^!_N:Ra_!Ra^!N\to N$,
$$\varepsilon^!_{\Lambda_s}\circ Ra_!(c)=\nu\circ\varepsilon^!_{\omega_s}.$$
These are equations of morphisms in the actual coefficient category at the chosen stage; the integral assertion concerns the specified completed composition comparison itself.

proof.text: At finite coefficients, [thm-sf-comp-composition] gives $\alpha_{\mathrm{id}_s,a}=vRa_!$ by its identity clause. Integrally the identity compactification in [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support] gives $IC=\mathcal L_s\mathcal R_sC$. Use the actual adjunction $\mathcal R_s\dashv\mathcal L_s$ and its unit $u$ from [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus]. The identity-open case of [lem-sf-integral-open-reduction-comparison] says that this $u_C$ is invertible on derived-complete inputs; the open coefficient comparison $r_{\mathrm{id}}$ is the identity, since extension by zero along the identity leaves the flat-term reduction representative and every quotient map unchanged. Its formula $d_{\mathrm{id}}=u_C^{-1}\mathcal L(r_{\mathrm{id}})^{-1}$ therefore fixes the canonical identity comparison as $v_C=u_C^{-1}$.

proof.text: Fix an integral input $K$ and a compactification $a=pj$ with $j$ quasi-compact open and $p$ proper. Put $T=S_pJ_j$ on semilinear systems, $N=T\mathcal R_XK$, and $C=d_{a,K}:\mathcal L_sN\xrightarrow{\sim}Ra_!K$, the direct strict-tower identification of [lem-sf-integral-compactification-comparison-bridge]. The tower is the one defining [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support]. The system inputs and intermediate outputs meet the realization domain of [lem-sf-integral-compactification-system-realization]: the datum's operations are on $D^b_{ctf}$, hence have common finite cohomological and Tor intervals, and (A5) of [def-sf-datum] identifies the system levels and quotient transitions with the finite reductions. Normalization and compatible etale-origin witnesses are part of the stated coefficient-domain data. Choose the outer identity compactification and retain the same compactification for the composite. The bridge lemma fixes $B_{\mathrm{id}}=1$, $I=\mathcal L_s\mathcal R_s$ and $d_{\mathrm{id},M}=1$ under the system unitors. It compares its counit formula to the actual word-normalized composition of [fix-lem-exchanges](2),(4); this is the comparison our statement names.

proof.text:
Write $e_N^{\mathrm{sys}}:\mathcal R_s\mathcal L_sN\to N$ for the actual system counit of [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus]. For the outer identity compactification, the proper/open map and proper/open compositors give $\beta=1_T$ by [lem-sf-ambient-proper-open-pasting]. Specialize the equality of [lem-sf-integral-compactification-comparison-bridge] to $(g,f)=(\mathrm{id}_s,a)$. Its $d_g=1$, $d_h=d_f=C$ and $B_g=1$ give, for the specified comparison of [fix-lem-exchanges](2),(4),
$$\alpha_{\mathrm{id}_s,a,K}=C\circ\mathcal L_s(e_N^{\mathrm{sys}})\circ\mathcal L_s\mathcal R_s(C^{-1}).$$
All maps here are actual integral maps. Naturality of $u$ gives $\mathcal L_s\mathcal R_s(C^{-1})u_{Ra_!K}=u_{\mathcal L_sN}C^{-1}$. The adjunction triangle $\mathcal L_s(e_N^{\mathrm{sys}})u_{\mathcal L_sN}=1$ therefore yields $\alpha_{\mathrm{id}_s,a,K}u_{Ra_!K}=1$. By Step 1, $u_{Ra_!K}$ is invertible, so $\alpha_{\mathrm{id}_s,a,K}=u_{Ra_!K}^{-1}=v_{Ra_!K}$. This uses the bridge's statement, without choosing or normalizing any of the unspecified expression-realization maps $c_V$.

proof.text: At $E$, [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi] has the same objects as the integral category and morphisms $f/t^r$; the higher compact-support operations are those of [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support]. Applying its scalar-localization functor $Q$ to Step 3 gives $\alpha_E=Q(\alpha_{\mathrm{int}})=Q(v_{Ra_!})=v_E Ra_{!,E}$. Here the operation/composition coefficient comparisons are the supplied compatibility data of (A5) of [def-sf-datum]. Naturality also holds on denominators: $v_{K'}I_E(f/t^r)=Q(v_{K'}I(f))/t^r=Q(fv_K)/t^r=(f/t^r)v_K$. At $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, choose one finite field containing representatives for the finitely many objects and morphisms in question, as in [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]. The equality just proved over that field gives equality of their common-stage classes. Under a further field extension the functor sends this equality and its inverse identities to the same equalities; (A5) identifies these images with the supplied operation/composition comparisons. This proves normalization at both field stages using the specified coefficient data, rather than deducing equality from reductions.

proof.text: Fix any of the four stages. Write $F=Ra_!$, $G=Ra^!$, $I=R\mathrm{id}_{s!}$ and $J=R\mathrm{id}_s^!$. Clause (A1) of [def-sf-datum] supplies $F\dashv G$, with unit $\eta$ and counit $\mu$, and $I\dashv J$, with counit $e:IJ\to\mathrm{id}$. Let $w_L=e_L\circ v_{JL}^{-1}:JL\to L$. Applying [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate] to $v^{-1}:\mathrm{id}\to I$, for $I\dashv J$ and the identity adjunction of [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction], gives precisely $w:J\to\mathrm{id}$: its component formula is $e_Lv_{JL}^{-1}$ because the identity-adjunction unit is the identity. That node says conjugation sends isomorphisms to isomorphisms, so $w$ is invertible. In particular $\nu=w_{\Lambda_s}$ is invertible. The maps $v_{\Lambda_s}:I\Lambda_s\to\Lambda_s$ and $\nu:J\Lambda_s\to\Lambda_s$ have different sources; the latter has just been constructed from $e$ and $v_{J\Lambda_s}^{-1}$.

source.place: Tag 0DV0, lemma-compose-counits, and the componentwise conjugation definition.

proof.text:
The preceding normalization says $\alpha=vF$. The counit of $IF\dashv GJ$ is $e_L\circ I(\mu_{JL})$ by [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]. Substitution in the conjugation formula of [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate] for $\alpha^{-1}:F\to IF$ gives
$$c_L=G(e_L)\circ G(I(\mu_{JL}))\circ G(v_{FGJL}^{-1})\circ\eta_{GJL}:GJL\longrightarrow GL.$$
Naturality of $v^{-1}:\mathrm{id}\to I$ at $\mu_{JL}:FGJL\to JL$ gives $I(\mu_{JL})\circ v_{FGJL}^{-1}=v_{JL}^{-1}\circ\mu_{JL}$. Thus
$$c_L=G(e_Lv_{JL}^{-1})\circ G(\mu_{JL})\circ\eta_{GJL}=G(w_L),$$
using the $F\dashv G$ triangle identity from (A1) of [def-sf-datum]. At $L=\Lambda_s$ this is $c=Ra^!(\nu)$; a functor carries the two inverse identities for $\nu$ to inverse identities for $c$, so $c$ is an isomorphism.

Steps 2–3 cite that formula from the new statement, including the identity compactification d=1, rather than from the proof of the realization lemma. Restores fix-lem-exchanges(2),(4) as the comparison named in the statement and used by the parents. The actual unit/counit triangle then proves identity normalization; Steps 1 and 4–7 are retained. One statement-only new node, no Mathlib leaves.
split_report.blueprint: The pairing-identification proof identifies the trace as the exceptional-adjunction counit. These steps supply its identity-point normalization; that calculation is agent-written and not claimed to appear in the blueprint.

tool_uses.why: Finite compact-support identity normalization is used as a generic composition tool; the identification unit has no construction of finite compact-support composition.
Its actual strict-tower, localized and common-stage compact-support functors fix the concrete objects and maps being normalized.
Its actual reduction/total-limit adjunction, unit, counit and triangle identities are needed for the completed identity calculation.
Its identity-open specialization fixes the inverse actual completion unit and proves its invertibility on derived-complete inputs.
The statement assumes this datum; its A1 and A5 provide precisely the adjunction and coefficient-compatibility structure used.
Its unital system compositors and identity proper/open maps compute the identity compactification before realization.
Its explicit localized Hom groups allow the equation and naturality to be checked on fractions.
Its common-stage morphism classes allow equality to be checked at the chosen finite coefficient field.
Its component formula and invertibility assertion compute the right identity comparison and composite mate.
Its identity adjunction and pasted counit formula type the conjugation calculations.
Only its stated normalized/common-bound system domains are used in Step 2. No normalization is inferred from its unspecified family c_V.

Its clauses (2),(4) specify the completed and transported composition comparison already used by the parent and sibling. The new bridge compares that same constant-tower word construction to the actual semilinear counit formula.
